answer: In each epoch the system opens an inlet of cryptographic challenges that require agents to generate a short sonnet‑style proof of work, forge a unique logical trace that only a genuine model can produce on demand. The verifier checks the fresh reasoning chain against a hash ledger; any identity that cannot supply the bespoke proof is discarded. Because every fake identity must expend full model inference for each challenge, the attacker’s cost scales linearly with the number of Sybils, quickly exceeding practical compute budgets.
